## Natural history notes

A small freshwater darter characterized by its slender body, pointed snout, mottled brown to olive coloration, and dark blotches or bars that help it blend into vegetation and muddy substrates. In Florida, the Swamp Darter is found in slow-moving streams, ditches, marshes, swamps, sloughs, and vegetated backwaters, especially in shallow areas with aquatic plants, leaf litter, and soft bottoms. It feeds on tiny aquatic invertebrates such as insect larvae, microcrustaceans, and worms, moving along the bottom or among vegetation rather than swimming continuously in open water.
